findings.where: Last section, 'Hostelworld, for comparison', which ends the page before the footer
findings.fault: The last thing a visitor reads is a named competitor, and Manta's case is made by contrast with it ('a hostel with a small recent base can look thin there'). Manta's method is the page's subject, but its closing impression is Hostelworld's weakness.
findings.who_objects: The founder. The brief's positioning says the claim Manta can safely make to travellers names no competitor. It also says Manta must not compete with Hostelworld, and a claim is held off the site while Hostelworld decides on Manta's application (#78). A backpacker who uses Hostelworld may also read the ending as a dig at a competitor rather than an honest method.

findings.where: First screen, the lede and the three-item numbered list under 'How we rank' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The promise that matters most, 'No hostel can pay for a higher position', is the first item in a small body-size list. The large lede above it only talks about the page ('We publish the method… This page states it in full'). At a squint, the heading and that lede win, and the line that earns trust looks like a footnote. The page also has no loud claim with calm mechanics under it, which is the move the brand asks for.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who arrives doubting that rankings are honest and gives the page five seconds. They leave without having taken in the one guarantee, because the largest words say there is a method, not what it promises.

findings.where: 'Ranking method' section: its four paragraphs (pay-independence, the pull toward the area average, review filtering and badges, review-count sort and the zero-review state). Also the 'Hostelworld, for comparison' paragraph
findings.fault: Four separate rules sit under one heading as 7- to 12-line blocks of text with no subheads or lead-ins. Each block is one long run of text and the key fact sits mid-paragraph ('Review count is never the default sort', 'Nothing is filtered from view'). The grouping is also wrong: the pull toward the area average and the review count both decide the score, but they sit under 'Ranking method', not 'Scoring method'. On a phone the section is about three screens of unbroken grey text.
findings.who_objects: A phone-first traveller scanning for one answer, such as 'do they hide bad reviews?' or 'why does this hostel with 3 reviews rank high?'. They cannot find it without reading everything, and the headings send them to the wrong section.

findings.where: Desktop, every section: the single text column against the left edge of the content area
findings.fault: At 1440 px the text runs in a narrow column on the left and about 60% of the width to its right is empty sand all the way down. Nothing sits there or balances it, so the page looks lopsided, like a draft document rather than a finished page on a brand site.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor on desktop deciding whether a pre-launch site is real. The lopsided, empty layout makes it look unfinished, and the brand names sterile as its enemy, which works against the trust the page exists to build.

findings.where: End of the page, after 'Hostelworld, for comparison' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: Once convinced, the visitor has nowhere to go. No line or link returns them to finding hostels (destinations), so the page ends on a competitor's help-centre citation, then the footer. On a phone the only way onward is the collapsed Menu at the top of a long page.
findings.who_objects: A traveller who came from a listing to check the ranking and now wants to get back to choosing a hostel. They have to scroll all the way back up and open the menu, and the trust the page built is lost at the moment it should lead to the search.

findings.where: Page as a whole: under the h1 and near the method sections
findings.fault: The published method carries no date or version ('method last changed …'). The only date on the page is when Hostelworld's help page was read. A method page that claims to state the rules 'in full' gives no way to tell whether they are current.
findings.who_objects: A careful visitor or a hostel owner checking whether today's rankings follow these rules. Without a date they cannot tell whether the method has changed since this page was written, and that weakens the 'we publish it' claim the page leads with.

findings.where: First screen: the lede, the summary sentence, the numbered list and the first line of 'Ranking method'
findings.fault: The opening says the same thing three times: a summary sentence, then a list restating it, then 'No hostel can pay for a higher position' again as the first sentence of the next section. The reader goes through the same points again before reaching anything new.
findings.who_objects: A visitor short on time. The repetition makes the first screen feel padded and pushes the real mechanics below the fold, on the phone in particular.
